title: Track: Import issues from Linear, Jira, GitHub Issues and CSV, and export a project to CSV
description:
Linear has guided importers for Jira, GitHub Issues, Asana, Shortcut and Linear itself that bring issues, projects, labels and users, with user mapping and an undo window (https://linear.app/docs/import-issues). Track has no importer and no export: a team switching over has to retype its backlog, which is the first reason not to switch. First scope: a CSV importer in Track › Settings with column mapping (title, description, status, priority, assignee by email, labels, due date, estimate, parent) into one project, plus a Linear importer using a personal API key (issues, comments, labels, states mapped by category) and a GitHub Issues importer per repo. Export: CSV of the current list view.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear, Jira.

title: Track: Update lists, board and issue pages live when a teammate changes something
description:
Linear syncs every change to every open client instantly. In Track the project list, board and issue page only change on reload: in a browser test, renaming an issue from a second session left the open list showing the old title after 15 seconds and a focus event (components/track/ProjectPageClient.tsx has no polling or subscription). Two people triaging the same board see different states and overwrite each other. First scope: a per-workspace change feed (SSE, or polling every few seconds while the tab is visible) carrying issue id + updated_at, merged into useIssueStore; refetch on window focus; on the issue page, show new comments and a notice when the description changed underneath an open editor.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Create issues from Slack messages and post issue activity to a Slack channel
description:
Linear's Slack integration creates an issue from any message (with a synced comment thread), posts team and project activity to a channel, sends personal notifications as DMs and unfurls issue links (https://linear.app/docs/slack). Track only reaches Slack if someone builds a Flow with the generic Slack node. First scope: one-click Slack connect in Track › Settings, a message shortcut "Create Track issue" that opens a modal with project, priority and assignee and links back to the message, per-project channel notifications for created / completed / commented, and unfurls for issue URLs.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add projects with lead, target date, health and written updates, plus a roadmap across them
description:
In Linear a project has a lead, members, start and target dates, status, and periodic updates marked On track / At risk / Off track with reminders to the lead (https://linear.app/docs/initiative-and-project-updates); initiatives group projects into a roadmap. A Track project is closer to a Linear team: it has milestones but no lead, target date, health or updates, and there is no view across projects. First scope: lead, target date and status on track_projects; a project update composer with health and auto-included progress since the last update; a weekly reminder to the lead; a roadmap page with one bar per project (start to target) and its latest health.

Priority: high. Effort: L. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Show cycle velocity, burn-up and cycle time so teams can plan the next cycle
description:
Linear Insights charts issue count and effort, cycle time, lead time, triage time and issue age, with slicing, segments and a burn-up, and exports to CSV (https://linear.app/docs/insights); cycles show scope and completion over time. Track's overview only shows done/total for the current cycle. First scope: on each cycle, a burn-up of scope vs completed points or issues (from the activity log), velocity of the last 3 completed cycles shown when creating the next one, and a cycle-time / lead-time panel per project with median and p75, using status category changes already logged in track activities.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear, Jira.

title: Track: Add private projects and guest members limited to the projects they are invited to
description:
Linear Business has private teams and guest accounts (https://linear.app/pricing); GitHub Projects and Jira have per-project permissions. In Track every workspace member sees and edits every project (canAccessTrackProject checks only the workspace), so teams that work with contractors or clients cannot use it. First scope: a project visibility setting (workspace / private with a member list), guest role that only sees projects they are added to and cannot see Cmd+K results or Inbox items from others, and enforcement in every /api/track route plus search and notifications.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear, Jira.

title: Track: Suggest labels, assignee and possible duplicates for issues in triage
description:
Linear Triage Intelligence proposes labels, assignee, project and duplicates for incoming issues (https://linear.app/pricing). Track's triage queue (issues from Chat, Flow, API, GitHub, Agents) is fully manual. First scope, only when AI is enabled for the workspace: on each triage issue, show suggested labels and assignee based on the last 200 accepted issues of the project, and the top 3 similar open issues by title and description with a one-click "Mark duplicate"; accept applies the suggestions in one click. Log which suggestions were accepted.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Link CRM companies and contacts to issues as customer requests
description:
Linear Customer Requests link feedback to issues and projects, show a customer page with every request, and let views sort issues by customer count, tier or revenue (https://linear.app/docs/customer-requests). zerosoft already has the CRM and Chat, so this can work without any third-party sync. First scope: a "Requested by" field on issues that links CRM companies or contacts (and the Chat conversation when created from Chat), a request count and summed deal value column in lists with sort, and a Track section on the CRM company page listing its requested issues and their status.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Set SLAs by priority and flag issues about to breach
description:
Linear supports issue SLAs and triage responsibility so urgent bugs get a response time (https://linear.app/pricing, Triage section); Jira Service Management triggers automations on SLA breach. Track has no response or resolution target. First scope: per-project SLA per priority (e.g. urgent 24 h, high 3 days) counted from creation or triage acceptance, a countdown chip on rows and the issue page, an "SLA" filter and sort, a notification to the assignee and project owner at 80 % and at breach, and an issue.sla_breached event for Flow.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Linear, Jira.

title: Track: Auto-close stale issues and auto-archive completed ones
description:
Linear lets each team auto-close issues untouched for N months and auto-archive completed issues after a period, which keeps lists short without manual cleanup (https://linear.app/docs). Track keeps every issue in its list forever unless deleted. First scope: per-project settings for auto-close (move to a cancelled status after 1, 3 or 6 months without activity, with a comment explaining why) and auto-archive (hide done/cancelled issues older than N months from default views, still searchable and restorable), run from the hourly cron with compare-and-set claims.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.
